disposition_reason: SEL capacity is finite and may use wrap, reject-new-entry or overflow-flag behavior. One append cannot reach or characterize that boundary, while an unbounded loop can erase or suppress real fault evidence. The literal raw payload must be known to be a harmless synthetic record so the resulting log is auditable. Because MC reset interrupts the very management plane being tested, reset type and reconnect evidence are distinct from SEL fullness. Cleanup must occur only after evidence capture and cannot be treated as an automatic recovery retry. test_case.test_name: Stress Test - Full SEL Volume — retained controlled review-layer procedure
test_case.purpose: Prove that the BMC handles a deliberately full System Event Log predictably, retains usable IPMI and Redfish management through the defined MC reset, and can be returned to a healthy logging state without losing required evidence.
required_package: SUT/BMC model, firmware and SEL implementation/capacity/overflow policy
Vendor-approved decoding and expected result of raw NetFn0x0a Cmd0x44 payload
Baseline SEL export location, protected real-event policy and synthetic-record identifier
Initial/free entry count, maximum append count, polling interval, full-state oracle, timeout and abort thresholds
Approved MC reset command/type, reconnect timeout and independent recovery path
Secure IPMI/Redfish endpoints plus post-full/post-reset health and approved cleanup/restoration procedure
test_case.test_command: Identify the BMC, SEL capacity/reservation/overflow behavior and meaning of the literal raw record; export existing SEL and capture baseline management health; obtain approval for one bounded fill operation and define count/full/timeout/abort; append the approved synthetic event while recording every response and periodic `sel info`; stop exactly at the approved full condition; capture full/overflow and record behavior; issue the separately approved MC reset; measure disconnect/reconnect and verify `mc info`, Redfish version/health and logging behavior; preserve all evidence, then run the approved SEL cleanup/restoration and verify capacity only after adjudication.

After SEL fullness, bmc command should work successfully."

safety_gate: Use only a dedicated non-production SUT and export/preserve all real SEL records before filling
Validate the exact raw record against the BMC specification; do not loop unexplained bytes
Bound the append count from verified capacity and stop on full, overflow, unexpected record, latency/error threshold or BMC instability
Do not clear SEL before full-state and post-reset evidence are reviewed; cleanup is not permission to hide failures
Require explicit approval for the management-disrupting MC reset and monitor reconnect through an independent path
Use injected credentials and verified target identity; do not expose passwords or disable identity checks
Never automatically retry a failed append/reset, power-cycle the SUT or improvise recovery
expected_evidence: BMC identity/firmware, SEL implementation/capacity/initial usage and exported baseline real records
Decoded raw event, approved synthetic marker and exact command/transport metadata
Every append result plus periodic record-count/free-space/full/overflow status and timestamps
Terminal full-state behavior including rejection/acceptance of the boundary append and preserved SEL export
Approved MC reset command, disconnect/reconnect timeline and post-reset `mc info` plus Redfish version/health
Post-reset SEL/logging behavior, cleanup/restoration transcript, final capacity/health and engineer verdict
